rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal performance. This configuration tests a standard multimodal setup with ViT (image encoder) and PCA (RNA encoder), which are common choices. It clarifies whether a basic multimodal approach outperforms single-modality models. This is the best use of the first experiment to set a reference point for comparison.

The existing evidence shows that the initial multimodal setup with pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l achieves 0.6287 accuracy. This experiment tests switching to transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could improve performance by leveraging more sophisticated interaction between modalities. It directly builds on the previous configuration while exploring critical design choices (aggregation/fusion) that significantly impact multimodal performance.

Existing evidence shows weighted fusion (config_020) outperforms concat (config_001) with 0.6352 vs 0.6287 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l (used in config_020) with resnet50 while maintaining weighted fusion. It clarifies whether the image encoder choice impacts performance when using the promising weighted fusion approach. This balances exploitation of the successful fusion method with exploration of alternative encoders, which could yield higher accuracy.

The existing evidence shows that using resnet50 image encoder with weighted fusion (config_010) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6389). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200, a more advanced model for scRNA-seq, while keeping the proven image encoder and fusion method. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice is a key factor in improving accuracy, balancing exploration of better encoders with exploitation of the current best setup.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_014) achieve high accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation, which could capture more complex interactions between modalities. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation improves performance on the same RNA/image encoder combination, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing components with exploration of aggregation methods.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders with transformer aggregation but uses concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, clarifying if fusion method choice is critical. It's a logical extension of the current best configuration, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of fusion method variations.

Existing evidence shows config_039 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_027), which shares the same image encoder and fusion method but uses a different RNA encoder. This clarifies whether scgpt could outperform scvi_n200 while maintaining the effective transformer aggregation and weighted fusion strategy. It balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of alternative encoders.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with the same aggregation/fusion setup to clarify if RNA encoder choice is critical. It reduces uncertainty about whether scvi_n200's superiority is robust or specific to its combination with resnet50. This is the best use of the remaining budget to validate key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_039) yield the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion to evaluate if the RNA encoder choice impacts performance. It clarifies whether scgpt could outperform scvi_n200 in this setup, leveraging the most promising components from prior experiments.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests the same RNA encoder and fusion method but with the imagenet_vit_l image encoder instead of resnet50, clarifying whether the image encoder choice impacts performance. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore a critical design choice with high potential for improvement.
